deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.16): X = P^1(C) - {0,1,inf} with the group Sigma generated by the anharmonic group S_3 (permuting a_0=0, a_1=1, a_inf=inf) and complex conjugation tau. The base point P is one of the two points e^{+-i pi/3}, both fixed by the order-3 Moebius map rho_bar: z -> 1/(1-z); Pbar is the other one. The 'groupe fondamental mixte' consists of pairs (gamma, path class from P to gamma^{-1}(P)), with paths composed like functions. The inverse image E of S_3 in it is an extension 1 -> pi_1(X,P) = F(l_0,l_1,l_inf) -> E -> S_3 -> 1. The page also refers to its profinite version E-hat.

Generators:
- l_i are the direct loops around a_i, with l_inf l_1 l_0 = 1 (relation (1), p.16).
- sigma_i lifts the transposition fixing a_i (and swapping the other two), using a half great circle from P to Pbar on the mirror of the reflection tau sigma_i.
- rho lifts rho_bar using the trivial path at P.

Relations (2): sigma_i^2 = 1; sigma_0 sigma_1 = rho l_0, sigma_1 sigma_inf = rho l_1, sigma_inf sigma_0 = rho l_inf. Consequently rho sigma_i rho^{-1} = sigma_{rho(i)}, i.e. rho permutes the sigma's cyclically 0 -> 1 -> inf.

Right margin: since sigma_1 = rho sigma_0 rho^{-1}, one gets l_0 = rho^{-1} sigma_0 rho sigma_0 rho^{-1} = rho^{-1}[sigma_0, rho]. Conjugation by sigma_0 acts by l_1 <-> l_inf and l_0 -> (l_1 l_inf)^{-1}.

Grothendieck observes that rho does not seem expressible through the sigma_i alone. He crosses out an attempted argument that rho must be a word in the sigma_i. He notes that the dotted relations (sigma_i^2 = 1, sigma_0 sigma_1 = sigma_1 sigma_inf = sigma_inf sigma_0 = rho, rho^3 = 1) present S_3. He then proposes that (1) + (2) + rho^3 = 1 present the inverse image of S_3 in Sigma (or E-hat). A left-margin note says 'C'est faux', with a test of the relation rho = 1.

Modern reading: X/S_3 is the j-line orbifold, with order-2 points at -1, 2, 1/2, an order-3 point at P, and a cusp. So E is the orbifold fundamental group, Z/2 * Z/3 = PSL_2(Z), containing pi_1(X) = image of Gamma(2) as a normal free subgroup of index 6. In the model, sigma_i are the three conjugate involutions and rho is the elliptic element of order 3. The page is a hand computation of an explicit presentation of this S_3-equivariant fundamental group, with base point at the order-3 point, as a preliminary to the next page. There Grothendieck introduces eps_i = l_i sigma_i l_{i+1}, with eps_i^2 = l_i, and seeks a presentation of an E^+ in terms of eps_i and rho.
errors: Right margin as transcribed, sigma_0(l_0) = l_0^{-1} l_1^{-1}, would equal l_inf by relation (1). That coincides with sigma_0(l_1) = l_inf, contradicting injectivity. The next page uses sigma_0(l_0) = (l_1 l_inf)^{-1} = l_inf^{-1} l_1^{-1}, which is conjugate to l_0 as it must be. So either the transcription or the margin has a slip.

The crossed-out idea that rho should be a product of the sigma_i is false. In Z/2*Z/3 the normal closure of the involutions has quotient Z/3, so rho is not in <sigma_0, sigma_1, sigma_inf>. Grothendieck's remark that no such expression appears is correct.

The left marginal 'C'est faux' appears to retract the presentation claim. However, (1) + (2) + rho^3 = 1 with sigma_i^2 = 1 does present Z/2*Z/3 = PSL_2(Z). One can check l_inf l_1 l_0 = 1 follows from sigma_0^2 = rho^3 = 1 and the conjugation rules. The objection may concern only a sub-claim or a test via rho = 1; the margin is too illegible to decide.
'défini par le chemin trivial de P à Pbar' must mean the trivial path at P, since rho_bar fixes P.

ideas.what: Explicit presentation of the S_3-equivariant (orbifold) fundamental group of P^1 - {0,1,inf}, based at the order-3 point e^{i pi/3}, with lifts sigma_i of transpositions and rho of the 3-cycle
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold pi_1 of the j-line, PSL_2(Z) = Z/2*Z/3 as an extension of S_3 by pi_1(M_{0,4}) (Gamma(2)/±1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Fricke–Klein); in Galois-theoretic form Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps; also Drinfeld's GT relations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Gamma_{0,4}, Gamma_{1,1} and S_3 symmetries qualitatively, not this computation

ideas.what: 'Mixed' fundamental group including complex conjugation tau and real-structure paths along mirror great circles
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental group of a real variety / pi_1 extended by Gal(C/R); tangential/symmetric base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 framework); real case studied later by Huisman, Nakamura and others
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions Gal(C/R) and real structures only briefly

ideas.what: Conjugation formulas l_0 = rho^{-1}[sigma_0, rho] and the action of sigma_0 on l_0, l_1, l_inf
ideas.modern_name: Action of the S_3 symmetries on F_2 (the substrate of the 2- and 3-cycle relations of GT)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine computation of a presentation of PSL_2(Z) viewed as the S_3-extension of the free group pi_1(P^1-{0,1,inf}) with a symmetric base point. It is of historical interest as Grothendieck's hands-on preparation for the S_3 / order-3 symmetry later encoded in GT. Nothing here is new or absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Right margin: 'sigma_0(l_0) = l_0^{-1} l_1^{-1}' is probably l_inf^{-1} l_1^{-1} (consistent with the next page's sigma_0(l_1 l_0) = l_1^{-1}).
Dotted system first line should read sigma_0-dot^2 = sigma_1-dot^2 = sigma_inf-dot^2 = 1 (the transcription repeats sigma_1-dot).
'en fonction des sigma_0, sigma_1, rho seuls' is likely 'sigma_0, sigma_1, sigma_inf seuls'.
Left margin reads roughly: 'C'est faux, comme on voit en annulant les l_i (?) ... relations rho=1, ... sigma_0 rho sigma_0^{-1} = sigma_1 (?)'; largely illegible.
